full_judgment: 13. This Court hereby declared the law, within the meaning of Article 111 of the Constitution of the Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh that is binding upon the Government as per Article 112 of the Constitution that, the question of possession of the property is miserably related to the question of title in the suit property. In anybody lacks lawful title in any property, then his or her obtaining and remaining in possession in that property or to get his/her name recorded in the khatain do not arise. The staffs working in the field survey operation cannot be indulged in the owner of a property shall remain standing in that place like a tree. In so many cases, owner of the property may not live in the property and he may stay at any other places or even in the abroad, but that does not authorizes a Government staff working in the field to record name of other person because of physical absence of the owner, when any title or other document to show that the Government has any right, title in the suit property is wanting. In order to write name of the Government in any khas khatian, the Government should or have some kind of document of title or some legal basis for claiming it as khas property of the Government, acquired by it or otherwise vested in it. Here, the person of the Government is as equal as any other ordinary person. The Government must have some basis or documents or other lawful sources to claim title in the concerned land in order to record its name in the khas khatian.
